name: HERON (radio)
full_name: Hybrid Elevated Radio Observatory for Neutrinos
summary: A planned hybrid radio observatory in Argentina combines compact phased stations with a sparse antenna array to search for ultra-high-energy tau neutrinos.
detection_principle: Earth-skimming tau neutrinos can interact in mountains and produce upward air showers. Dense phased arrays lower the radio threshold while separated autonomous antennas constrain shower geometry.

status.label: Research and development
status.evidence: Funding selection and site-development work are documented; full science-array operation remains a future phase.

timeline.event: Concept study released and ERC Synergy funding selected.
Local project page describes site-characterisation campaigns and consortium preparation.

collaboration.name: HERON Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Preliminary layout
key_parameters.value: 24 phased stations with 24 antennas each, plus 360 standalone antennas

key_parameters.name: Terrain
key_parameters.value: A roughly 72 km mountain range in San Juan Province

key_parameters.name: Projected elevation
key_parameters.value: An elevation of approximately 1,000 m in the preliminary layout, along a 72-km mountain range overlooking a valley

results.summary: Hybrid sensitivity and reconstruction studies motivate the funded development; no full HERON science exposure is claimed.

science_scope: This Argentine radio-array project is distinct from the historical superfluid-helium solar-neutrino proposal also called HERON. Design parameters and sensitivities are forecasts, not observations.
